quotes.passage: We propose a new test to measure a text model’s multitask accuracy.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes a test intended to measure the multitask accuracy of text models.

quotes.passage: The test covers 57 tasks including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science, law, and more.
quotes.statement: The paper states that the test covers 57 tasks, including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science and law.

quotes.passage: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers.
quotes.statement: The paper introduces a language representation model called BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers).

quotes.passage: This paper examines the potential impact of artificial intelligence (A.I.) on economic growth.
quotes.locator: NBER Working Paper 23928, PDF p. 2, abstract
quotes.statement: The paper states that it examines the potential impact of artificial intelligence on economic growth.

quotes.passage: The goal throughout is to refine a set of critical questions about A.I. and economic growth and to contribute to shaping an agenda for the field.
quotes.locator: NBER Working Paper 23928, PDF p. 2, abstract
quotes.statement: The authors state that their goal is to refine a set of questions about artificial intelligence and economic growth and to contribute to an agenda for the field.

quotes.passage: We present a list of five practical research problems related to accident risk, categorized according to whether the problem originates from having the wrong objective function … an objective function that is too expensive to evaluate frequently … or undesirable behavior during the learning process …
quotes.statement: The paper presents five practical research problems related to accident risk in machine learning systems, grouped by whether they originate from a wrong objective function, an objective function too expensive to evaluate frequently, or undesirable behaviour during learning.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we show that commonsense inference still proves difficult for even stateof-the-art models, by presenting HellaSwag, a new challenge dataset.
quotes.statement: The paper presents HellaSwag, a challenge dataset, and states that it shows commonsense inference remains difficult for the strongest models it tested.

quotes.passage: To help address this concern, we propose training agents via self play on a zero sum debate game.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes training agents via self-play on a zero-sum debate game, as a way to address tasks too complicated for a human to judge directly.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we introduce a simpler and more effective approach, enabling the translation of rare and unknown words by encoding them as sequences of subword units…
quotes.statement: The paper introduces an approach to translating rare and unknown words in neural machine translation by encoding them as sequences of subword units, which it describes as simpler and more effective than back-off dictionaries.

quotes.passage: We apply preference modeling and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to finetune language models to act as helpful and harmless assistants.
quotes.statement: The paper describes applying preference modelling and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to fine-tune language models to act as helpful and harmless assistants.

quotes.passage: The paper develops a growth model that features Singularity and presents several tests of whether we are rapidly approaching Singularity.
quotes.locator: NBER Working Paper 21547, PDF p. 3, abstract
quotes.statement: The paper states that it develops a growth model featuring what it labels Singularity and presents several tests of whether the economy is rapidly approaching it.

quotes.passage: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million high-resolution images in the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 contest into the 1000 different classes.
quotes.statement: The authors state that they trained a large, deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million images of the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 contest into 1000 classes.

quotes.passage: This paper introduces MMLU-Pro, an enhanced dataset designed to extend the mostly knowledge-driven MMLU benchmark by integrating more challenging, reasoning-focused questions and expanding the choice set from four to ten options.
quotes.statement: The paper introduces MMLU-Pro, a dataset that extends the MMLU benchmark with more reasoning-focused questions and expands the answer choices from four to ten.

quotes.passage: We present a new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
quotes.statement: The paper presents a question set, text corpus and baselines, together called the AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC), intended to encourage research in advanced question answering.

quotes.passage: We are also releasing the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task, and implementations of the three neural baseline models tested.
quotes.statement: The authors state that they release the ARC Corpus of 14M science sentences and implementations of the three neural baseline models they tested.

quotes.passage: the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context
quotes.statement: The paper presents C-Eval, an evaluation suite for the knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context, which it states is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite.
quotes.auditNote: Shortened after audit A: the text layer splits the small-capital name "C-EVAL" ("C-E VAL"), so the name is left out of the quotation.

quotes.passage: We propose a simple way to resolve this issue by decoupling weight decay and the optimization steps taken w.r.t. the loss function.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes decoupling weight decay from the optimization steps taken with respect to the loss function, to resolve what it describes as a limitation of common implementations of adaptive gradient algorithms such as Adam.

quotes.passage: In this work, we present GNMT, Google’s Neural Machine Translation system, which attempts to address many of these issues.
quotes.statement: The paper presents GNMT, Google’s Neural Machine Translation system, which it describes as an attempt to address the computational cost and rare-word robustness issues of neural machine translation.

quotes.passage: To address the former challenge, we present an algorithm capable of learning arbitrary nonlinear cost functions, such as neural networks, without meticulous feature engineering.
quotes.statement: The paper presents an inverse optimal control algorithm that it states can learn arbitrary nonlinear cost functions, such as neural networks, without meticulous feature engineering.

quotes.passage: To address the latter challenge, we formulate an efficient sample-based approximation for MaxEnt IOC.
quotes.statement: The paper formulates a sample-based approximation for maximum-entropy inverse optimal control, addressing cost learning under unknown dynamics.

quotes.passage: We present LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications.
quotes.statement: The paper presents LaMDA (Language Models for Dialog Applications).

quotes.passage: LaMDA is a family of Transformerbased neural language models specialized for dialog, which have up to 137B parameters and are pre-trained on 1.56T words of public dialog data and web text.
quotes.statement: The paper describes LaMDA as a family of Transformer-based language models specialised for dialog, with up to 137B parameters, pre-trained on 1.56T words of public dialog data and web text.

quotes.passage: To further our understanding of the impact of scale on few-shot learning, we trained a 540-billion parameter, densely activated, Transformer language model, which we call Pathways Language Model (PaLM).
quotes.statement: The authors state that, to study the impact of scale on few-shot learning, they trained a 540-billion-parameter, densely activated Transformer language model called Pathways Language Model (PaLM).

quotes.passage: We investigate various methods to encode positional information in transformer-based language models and propose a novel implementation named Rotary Position Embedding(RoPE).
quotes.statement: The paper examines methods of encoding positional information in transformer-based language models and proposes an implementation it names Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE).

quotes.passage: I n the following pages an attempt is made to take more of the magic out of the brain by means of a “subassembly” theory, which is a modification of Hebb’s famous speculative cell-assembly theory.
quotes.statement: Good states that the text attempts to take more of the magic out of the brain by means of a “subassembly” theory, which he describes as a modification of Hebb’s cell-assembly theory.

quotes.passage: We examine the concerns that new technologies will render labor redundant in a framework in which tasks previously performed by labor can be automated and new versions of existing tasks, in which labor has a comparative advantage, can be created.
quotes.locator: publisher page (American Economic Review), page text, abstract
quotes.statement: The authors state that they examine concerns that new technologies will render labor redundant, using a framework in which tasks performed by labor can be automated and new tasks in which labor has a comparative advantage can be created.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we describe XGBoost, a scalable machine learning system for tree boosting.
quotes.locator: arXiv v1, PDF p. 1, §1 Introduction, para. 3
quotes.statement: The paper describes XGBoost, a scalable machine learning system for tree boosting.

quotes.passage: We propose a novel sparsity-aware algorithm for sparse data and weighted quantile sketch for approximate tree learning.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes a sparsity-aware algorithm for sparse data and a weighted quantile sketch for approximate tree learning.

quotes.passage: We refer to this phenomenon as internal covariate shift, and address the problem by normalizing layer inputs.
quotes.statement: The paper names the change in each layer’s input distribution during training internal covariate shift and states that it addresses the problem by normalizing layer inputs.

quotes.passage: In this work, we focus on channels and propose a novel architectural unit, which we term the “Squeeze-and-Excitation”(SE) block, that adaptively recalibrates channel-wise feature responses by explicitly modelling interdependencies between channels.
quotes.statement: The paper proposes an architectural unit, the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) block, which it states adaptively recalibrates channel-wise feature responses by modelling interdependencies between channels.

quotes.passage: In order to address this issue, we introduce an extension to the encoder–decoder model which learns to align and translate jointly.
quotes.locator: arXiv v1, PDF p. 1, §1 Introduction, para. 4
quotes.statement: The paper introduces an extension to the encoder–decoder model for neural machine translation that learns to align and translate jointly, as a way to address an issue it identifies with encoding a source sentence into a fixed-length vector.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we propose a novel neural network model called RNN Encoder–Decoder that consists of two recurrent neural networks (RNN).
quotes.statement: The paper proposes a neural network model called RNN Encoder–Decoder, consisting of two recurrent neural networks.

quotes.passage: We present a class of efficient models called MobileNets for mobile and embedded vision applications.
quotes.statement: The paper presents a class of models called MobileNets, intended for mobile and embedded vision applications.

quotes.passage: In this paper, we present a general end-to-end approach to sequence learning that makes minimal assumptions on the sequence structure.
quotes.statement: The paper presents a general end-to-end approach to sequence learning that, according to the authors, makes minimal assumptions on the sequence structure.
